Name: Dragonbay
Summary: A third-person platformer that couples Neurofeedback with motoric challenges

Description.Text:
Dragonbay is a third-person platformer that combines classical controller-based gameplay with Neurofeedback. In it the player controls a dragon who has to traverse various levels facing numerous challenges along the way. Each level's floor is split into cube-shaped tiles which the player has to raise from the water below by maintaining positive Neurofeedback. Should the player's feedback become negative, the tiles will start to move and rotate, trying to shake them off. If the player falls into the water, they will respawn at the last checkpoint they reached. The player also has two main tools/abilities at their disposal: Jumping to cross gaps and a fire breath to burn/melt obstacles as well as activate certain lever-like mechanics. In the course of the gameplay players also obtain Neuro Coins which they can spend to unlock additional dragons. These dragons have further abilities, such as double jumps and stat enhancements, or even gameplay modifiers like gliding.
When I started working on Dragonbay it had not been updated in quite some time. After updating its visuals and rebuilding various of its systems (such as character movement, level design tools, etc.) I expanded the original 20 levels in its classic pirate bay and mountain/volcano themes with 2 more 'basic' levels per environment as well as an entirely new norse/ice world. I also reworked some its slightly outdated levels to provide players with a fresh experience. Due to the constantly expanding scope of the project it took slightly longer than originally anticipated, but the additional time was worth it: Dragonbay was very well received by our clients, both in our Munich practice as well as with our Software customers globally.

Name: BrainAssistant
Summary: The main software developed and distributed by brainboost. It is capable of Neurofeedback, qEEG recordings, advanced EEG analysis, and much more

Description.Text:
The BrainAssistant is a highly advanced & professional application for Neurofeedback, qEEG recordings, advanced EEG analysis, and much more. It is compatible with most well-known EEG amplifiers and provides a combination of features, quality, and modern design not found elsewhere in the EEG-related industry.
Mostly developed by our CTO Daniel, I've also contributed to and sometimes created various features. The most noticeable ones include Telemetry, data exports for research projects and university partners, as well as a lot of smaller features for our game-related data handling & evaluation, but also overall code maintenance, QoL features, and bug fixing.

Name: NeuroRacer
Summary: A fast-paced racing game where the player must maintain positive Neurofeedback in order to accelerate

Description.Text:
NeuroRacer is the first full project I got to work on by myself. The underlying concept involves the player driving along a road and racing against NPC opponents. Acceleration is achieved via positive Neurofeedback, while steering is done via controller/keyboard inputs. In order to simplify the game principle and make it accessible to a wider audience the player does not have to fully steer the car. Instead, the car drives automatically along its current lane and steering is only required to swap lanes.
In its original state the project only existed as a simple proof-of-concept where the player would drive along a single, straight road. I rebuilt the project from the ground up and added curves as well as other dynamic segments by adding a fully fleshed out procedural generation system. Later, I also added some entirely new environments, more cars, and a Nitro-boost (also charged via positive feedback).
The core design for the environments saw NeuroRacer as a kind of 'Multiverse' or cross-over game that would have the player visit some areas already known from our other games, such as the 'Asia' environment from Focus Master or the 'Pirates' environment from Dragonbay.

Name: Pirate Islands
Summary: A walking simulator that takes the player on a treasure hunt across the seas

Description.Text: Another project I worked on was Pirate Islands. This game is a kind of walking simulator where the player traverses various environments (represented as treasure maps) by maintaining positive Neurofeedback. Treasure map routes are split into various sub-elements like sailing or walking segments. Occasional hazards may also block the path, requiring special effort to continue. Initially the project was created with only its original route mind, so I updated it use a more modular & extendable system, similar to one big cutscene editor. Afterwards I added a number of new routes, also containing nods to various other brainboost games. See the images below for some examples.
